# Governed Workbook Contract

`scripts/build.py` runs `scripts/validate_cases.py` first, then uses `scripts/common.py` to enforce/render this automatically. Load this file only when the user asks about the format or a supplied reference workbook conflicts with it.

## Sheets (in order)
1. **Dashboard** — Overall, User Story/Module-wise, Test Category-wise, Priority-wise summaries. Columns: Summary, Total Test Cases, [Active Platform Columns: e.g. Mobile App, Web, Mobile App+Web — dynamically generated matching the exact platforms detected in test cases], Not Executed, Pass, Fail, Blocked, Skip, NA, On Hold, Deferred, Pass %. A story-update workbook replaces Total Test Cases with Previous Total and Updated Total, and adds Existing, New, Modified, Invalidated before Pass %.
2. **Automation Dashboard** — same structure; only `Automation Candidate = Yes` rows; buckets from the distinct `Automation Status` column. Columns: Summary, Total Automation Candidates, [Active Platform Columns: e.g. Mobile App, Web, Mobile App+Web — dynamically generated matching the exact platforms detected in test cases], Not Executed, Pass, Fail, Blocked, Skip, NA, Test Data Dependency, Pass %. On a story update, Previous Total and Updated Total replace the single total and reference the Dashboard automation counts.
3. **iOS Dashboard** — Generated ONLY when the project platform supports iOS (`Both Android and iOS`, `iOS`, or multi-platform combinations with Mobile App: `Mobile App + Web`, `Mobile App + Mobile Web`, `Mobile App + Web + Mobile Web`). For `Android`, `Web`, `Mobile Web`, and `Web + Mobile Web`, the iOS Dashboard tab is NOT created in the Excel workbook. When created, mirrors the manual Dashboard, but every formula counts only rows where `IOS Testcase = Yes`; buckets use the normal manual `Status` column. Columns: Summary, Total iOS Test Cases, Not Executed, Pass, Fail, Blocked, Skip, NA, On Hold, Deferred, Pass % (Mobile App, Web, and Mobile Web platform columns are not generated in the iOS Dashboard tab). On a story update, Previous Total and Updated Total replace the single total and reference the Dashboard iOS counts.
4. **Config** — dropdown sources: Status, Test Category, Type, Priority, Automation Candidate, Regression Candidate, [IOS Testcase — if platform supports iOS], Automation Status, Source Type, Test Data Status *(and Test Case Type in Brownfield mode)*. Named ranges back list validation on governed sheets.
5. **Test Data Requirements** — one consolidated, semantically deduplicated list of actionable data prerequisites with user story traceability across 9 columns: `Test Data ID` · `User Story ID` · `User Story / Module` · `Test Data Description` · `Required For` · `Requirement Reference` · `Data Setup / Preparation Notes` · `Environment / Platform` · `Status`. One row per unique data state, not per testcase. Do not include actual credentials, passwords, account numbers, PII, or secret values. `Required For` contains the impacted scenario/module label(s). Status values: `Not Prepared`, `Requested`, `In Progress`, `Available`, `Blocked`; design-stage default is `Not Prepared`.
6. **One sheet per User Story/module** (title row, meta row, header row 3, data from row 4).

## Testcase columns (exact order)
**Standalone Mode — Mode A: GREENFIELD:**
- **With iOS Column (27 Columns)** — Applicable for `Both Android and iOS`, `iOS`, `Mobile App + Web`, `Mobile App + Mobile Web`, `Mobile App + Web + Mobile Web`:
  Module · Test Scenario ID · Test Scenarios · Test Case ID · Test Description · Requirement Reference · Priority (P0/P1/P2) · Pre-condition · Type (Positive/Negative/Edge Case) · Test Steps · Test Data · Expected Result · Test Category · **Platform** · Actual Result · Status · Automation Candidate (Yes/No) · Regression Candidate (Yes/No) · **IOS Testcase** · Source Type · Remarks · **BA Comments** · **Developer Status** · **Developer Comment** · Automation Status · Actual Automation Result · Automation Remark (final).
- **Without iOS Column (26 Columns)** — Applicable for `Android`, `Web`, `Mobile Web`, `Web + Mobile Web`:
  Module · Test Scenario ID · Test Scenarios · Test Case ID · Test Description · Requirement Reference · Priority (P0/P1/P2) · Pre-condition · Type (Positive/Negative/Edge Case) · Test Steps · Test Data · Expected Result · Test Category · **Platform** · Actual Result · Status · Automation Candidate (Yes/No) · Regression Candidate (Yes/No) · Source Type · Remarks · **BA Comments** · **Developer Status** · **Developer Comment** · Automation Status · Actual Automation Result · Automation Remark (final).
*(Note: Standalone Greenfield strictly prohibits `Test Case Type` and `TestCaseTypeList` defined name in Config).*

**Update Modes — Mode B: BROWNFIELD, Mode C: GREENFIELD With Updated User Story, & Mode D: Brownfield — Existing App, From Scratch:**
- **With iOS Column (28 Columns)** — Applicable for `Both Android and iOS`, `iOS`, `Mobile App + Web`, `Mobile App + Mobile Web`, `Mobile App + Web + Mobile Web`:
  Module · Test Scenario ID · Test Scenarios · Test Case ID · Test Description · Requirement Reference · Priority (P0/P1/P2) · Pre-condition · Type (Positive/Negative/Edge Case) · Test Steps · Test Data · Expected Result · Test Category · **Platform** · Actual Result · Status · Automation Candidate (Yes/No) · Regression Candidate (Yes/No) · **IOS Testcase** · **Test Case Type** · Source Type · Remarks · **BA Comments** · **Developer Status** · **Developer Comment** · Automation Status · Actual Automation Result · Automation Remark (final).
- **Without iOS Column (27 Columns)** — Applicable for `Android`, `Web`, `Mobile Web`, `Web + Mobile Web`:
  Module · Test Scenario ID · Test Scenarios · Test Case ID · Test Description · Requirement Reference · Priority (P0/P1/P2) · Pre-condition · Type (Positive/Negative/Edge Case) · Test Steps · Test Data · Expected Result · Test Category · **Platform** · Actual Result · Status · Automation Candidate (Yes/No) · Regression Candidate (Yes/No) · **Test Case Type** · Source Type · Remarks · **BA Comments** · **Developer Status** · **Developer Comment** · Automation Status · Actual Automation Result · Automation Remark (final).

**Deletion Mode — Mode E: Delete user story tab (Mode E):**
Preserves the source workbook's column structure (27 columns if source was Greenfield, 28 columns if source had Test Case Type) across all remaining sheets. Test cases in remaining sheets are preserved as-is. Dashboards recalculate dynamically.

Values: Priority P0/P1/P2 · Type Positive/Negative/Edge Case · Category Functional, Field Validation, UI, Compatibility, Usability · Platform mobile app, web, mobile web, or combinations (e.g. mobile app, web; mobile app, mobile web; web, mobile web; mobile app, web, mobile web) — do not hallucinate unsupported platforms · Status Not Executed, Pass, Fail, Skip, NA, Blocked, On Hold, Deferred · Automation Candidate Yes/No (governed by Automation Candidate Yes/No Decision Rules 1–8: SHOULD_BE_YES and CONDITIONAL_YES map to Yes; BLOCKED_REQUIREMENT and CORRECT_NO map to No; prerequisites, feasibility limitations, and bold title `**No automation reason:** <reason>` documented in Remarks ONLY; Automation Remark remains blank during generation) · Regression Candidate Yes/No · IOS Testcase Yes/No · Test Case Type (Update modes only: existing, modified, new, invalidated) · Source Type SOURCE/DERIVED/ADVISORY/BLOCKED · BA Comments recorded for BA review notes/clarifications · Developer Status & Developer Comment tracked for development updates · Automation Status Not Executed, Pass, Fail, Skip, NA, Blocked, Test Data Dependency · Test Data Status Not Prepared, Requested, In Progress, Available, Blocked. `fail` is normalized to `Fail`.

**Platform & Dashboard platform count contract:**
Every test case sheet includes the `Platform` column positioned immediately before `Actual Result` (immediately after `Test Category`). The `Platform` column contains the actual platform on which the testcase can be executed, governed by the Automation Types definitions:
- **Mobile:** What is tested: *Native apps installed from an `.apk` / `.ipa`* | Runs on: *Real Android and iOS devices, emulators and simulators*.
- **Web:** What is tested: *The website in a desktop browser* | Runs on: *Chromium (Chrome, Edge), Firefox, WebKit (Safari engine)*.
- **Mobile Web:** What is tested: *The web app as a phone user opens it: in the mobile browser, or installed to the home screen* | Runs on: *Chrome on Android, Safari on iOS (real devices)*.
Allowed cell values: `Mobile App`, `Web`, `Mobile Web`, or combinations thereof (e.g. `Mobile app, Mobile Web`, `Mobile App, Web`, `Web, Mobile Web`, `Mobile App, Web, Mobile Web`). For example, if a testcase is runnable on Mobile App and Mobile Web, `Web` is not shown in this column. Never display unapplicable platforms.
Dashboard and Automation Dashboard sheets include dedicated columns for each distinct platform detected in the Platform column of test cases (e.g. `Mobile App`, `Web`, `Mobile App+Web`). If a test case supports a combination of platforms (e.g. `Mobile App+Web`), it receives its own dedicated column rather than double counting across individual platforms. Live formulas report platform-specific test case counts such that each test case increments exactly one platform column, ensuring the sum of platform columns equals exactly the Total Test Cases count. Platform columns are strictly generated for Dashboard and Automation Dashboard, and are not generated in the iOS Dashboard tab.

**BA Comments column contract:**
The `BA Comments` column is placed immediately before `Developer Status` (following `Remarks`). It is reserved for Business Analyst notes, clarification tracking, and requirement alignment comments.

**Test Data column contract:** Must contain concrete, realistic sample data reflecting exact requirement combinations and rules (e.g., PAN ID: `PAN ID: AYNMH8765J`; password combination `Adhi@23435g`). Where no test data is possible or needed (e.g., navigation, viewing static screens, back button, screen orientation), keep completely empty (`""`). Never use random data, generic placeholders (`Synthetic valid test data`, `Invalid test inputs`, `N/A`), or test data ID references (`TD1`, `TD2`, `TD-001`). Distinct from Sheet 5 (`Test Data Requirements`) which tracks environment prerequisites.

**Runtime file integrity contract:** Most importantly, the generated files should not be edited during runtime of skill. Never manually modify, mutate, or edit generated script files, JSON data, or output Excel workbooks during runtime execution. Everything must be generated directly and deterministically by the skill execution pipeline via `cases.json` and `scripts/build.py`.

## Formulas
Live, never hardcoded. Module rows: `COUNTA` total, `COUNTIF` per manual status; automation: `COUNTIF(candidate,"Yes")` and `COUNTIFS(candidate,"Yes",autoStatus,"<status>")`; iOS: `COUNTIF(IOS Testcase,"Yes")` and `COUNTIFS(IOS Testcase,"Yes",Status,"<status>")`. Overall = module Total row (single reconciliation path). Category/Priority = `COUNTIFS` summed across module sheets. `Pass % = IF(Total=0,0,Pass/Total)`. On a story update, that Total is Updated Total (Existing + Modified + New); Previous Total is the fixed original count. Ranges extend to row 5000 so later execution updates are included. Sheet names sanitized/truncated to 31 chars before formulas are written. If the user wants an execution-only denominator, state the rule explicitly rather than silently changing the formula.


## Preflight governance validation (hard gate)
Before any `.xlsx` is created, `validate_cases.py` must report zero errors. It enforces: non-empty/unique Scenario IDs and Test Case IDs; Requirement Reference on SOURCE/DERIVED/BLOCKED; valid Config enums; `Not Executed` as the design-stage status; BLOCKED → `TBD` + `RQ-...`; no blank core fields (scenario, description, steps, expected result); explicit Yes/No regression classification; explicit Yes/No `IOS Testcase` classification; explicit Yes/No automation classification governed by Decision Rules 1–8 (with Remarks containing bold title `**No automation reason:** <reason>` with concrete domain explanation for every No, and Automation Remark kept blank). Any error aborts the build.

## Verification (build.py does this)
Structural: Dashboard/Automation Dashboard/iOS Dashboard/Config/Test Data Requirements present; COUNTIF/COUNTIFS families present; `"Yes"` filter and `Test Data Dependency` formula on Automation Dashboard; no literal `#REF!`. Recalc: LibreOffice headless, scan every cell for `#REF! #DIV/0! #VALUE! #NAME? #N/A`. Reconciliation: overall totals = sum of module totals; automation candidate total = count of Automation Candidate=Yes rows; iOS total = count of IOS Testcase=Yes rows. Coverage: design/executable/automation-design layers, likely duplicates, vague expected results.

## Scope rules & Reviewer Standard Quality Gates
Manual/black-box unless API/backend design is requested — no Postman, direct API calls, DB queries, payload inspection in manual steps; backend-only requirements keep traceability with the limitation in Remarks. `Negative` is a Type, not a Category. `Source Type` is maintained strictly in its dedicated column and is never embedded in Remarks. Deliver ONE workbook.
Every test case must contain all 13 core attributes: Module, Test Scenario ID, Test Scenario, Test Case ID, Test Description, Requirement Reference, Priority, Preconditions, Type, Test Steps, Test Data, Expected Result, Test Category.
Expected results must be specific, measurable, and verifiable. Statements such as "System should work correctly", "User should get proper response", and "Application should behave as expected" are strictly prohibited.
Cryptic shorthand codes (e.g. screen codes S1, S2, error codes E01, E02, button/page codes) must NOT be displayed in the generated Excel test cases; they must be completely replaced with full descriptions from the user story (e.g. display 'Login Basic screen' instead of 'S1'). Generic terms like 'step 1' or 'page 1' must be resolved to their actual action or referenced description (e.g. 'Click on continue button' instead of 'step 1'). All narrative columns (Test Steps, Pre-condition, Expected Result, Test Description, Test Scenarios, Remarks) must be written in simple, clear language understandable by any person.
In update modes, Modified cases must have their specific change reasons recorded in Remarks (never modify for wording changes alone), Invalidated cases must have removal evidence recorded in Remarks, and historical test cases are never deleted.
An internal Requirement Coverage Matrix (`Requirement ID | Acceptance Criteria | Existing Test Case | Comparison Result | Gap / Action`) must be validated before workbook generation. A requirement is never marked fully covered if any applicable acceptance criterion remains uncovered.


## Greenfield / Brownfield and platform scope
Greenfield workbooks (Mode A) contain full approved-scope coverage created from scratch without a test bank. When updating an existing test bank (Modes B, C, D — modes other than Greenfield), the designated test bank is copied AS IS in the generated Excel workbook: all existing module sheets and test data requirements are preserved/copied into the generated copy. ONLY the user story given in the BRD is updated with test cases (updating its matching sheet, or adding it as a new sheet if new). In Claude Projects, Project Context/project knowledge is part of the review set when accessible. `IOS Testcase` is a selective execution flag: Yes for important/platform-sensitive iOS scenarios, No otherwise; do not clone the full suite for iOS.

## Story-update sheets and counts
When updating an existing test bank (Modes B, C, D), the output is a separate workbook copy (`--out` must differ from `source_workbook`). The designated test bank is copied AS IS: all existing sheets/modules from the designated test bank are retained in the workbook, and ONLY the user story given in the BRD is updated with the test cases. Each sheet in update modes holds `existing`, `modified`, `invalidated`, and `new`. Unchanged copied sheets retain their test cases marked `existing`. Updated Total = Existing + Modified + New and excludes Invalidated. Updated and status counts are live formulas. Pass % uses Updated Total as the denominator. The Automation Dashboard and iOS Dashboard previous and updated totals reference the matching Dashboard cells, and reflect all module sheets across the workbook.

## Mode E: Story Deletion and Dashboard Recalculation
When deleting a user story tab (Mode E), the designated story/sheet is omitted from the generated workbook. Any prerequisite in `Test Data Requirements` whose `Required For` lists only the deleted story is removed; shared prerequisites have the deleted story removed from `Required For`. All three dashboards (`Dashboard`, `Automation Dashboard`, `iOS Dashboard`) dynamically generate summary and module rows pointing strictly to the remaining sheets, recalculating all overall, module, category, and priority totals via live formulas. Output is always written to a separate workbook copy (`--out`).


## iOS Dashboard
`iOS Dashboard` is generated ONLY when the project platform supports iOS (`Both Android and iOS`, `iOS`, or multi-platform combinations with Mobile App: `Mobile App + Web`, `Mobile App + Mobile Web`, `Mobile App + Web + Mobile Web`). For `Android`, `Web`, `Mobile Web`, and `Web + Mobile Web`, the `iOS Dashboard` tab is NOT created.
When generated:
- It mirrors the manual Dashboard layout. All Overall, module-wise, category-wise, priority-wise, and status counts must be formula-filtered to rows where `IOS Testcase = Yes`. Its status buckets use the manual `Status` column.
- If platform is `iOS`: Every entry in the `IOS Testcase` column must be `Yes` across all test cases.
- Pass % is iOS Pass / the iOS total, and on a story update that denominator is the iOS Updated Total. Story-update previous and updated totals reference the Dashboard. Mobile App, Web, and Mobile Web columns are not generated in the iOS Dashboard tab. It must remain dynamic when testcase flags or statuses change.

## Independent QA Review & Single Final Workbook Delivery Contract
During the Independent QA Review phase:
1. For each input user story document, the skill must deliver strictly ONE final Excel workbook (e.g. `reports/<Name>_TestCases_v1_0.xlsx`). Two different Excel files (such as an uncorrected copy and a corrected copy, or a separate regression file) must NOT be output for the same document.
2. When multiple input user story docs are provided in the user story user input section, the number of output Excel workbooks generated must be exactly the same as the number of input documents. Every input document must generate its own separate test case Excel workbook (1:1 Document-to-Workbook mapping).
3. When gap recovery is performed, all recovered test cases and unrecoverable gap notes are incorporated directly into the single final deliverable workbook for that document.
4. Existing test cases must not be silently modified or deleted.
5. All recovered test cases must populate all mandatory columns (27 for Greenfield, 28 for Update modes), maintain correct Requirement Reference, Source Type, Priority, Category, and Platform, and record recovery details in the `Remarks` column per the standard (`[Gap Recovery - RECOVERED]`, `[Gap Recovery - UNRECOVERABLE]`, `[Gap Recovery - ADR CONTRADICTION]`, `[Gap Recovery - DEFECT CORRECTED]`).
6. A review report table (`Gap ID | Requirement ID | Test Case ID | Gap Description | Recovery Status | Recovery Action | Remarks`) and G01–G14 review controls validation are delivered alongside each final workbook.
